2608.25553.title: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked: Budgeted Verification Failures in Inherited Agent Memory
2608.25553.paper_summary: An agent that inherits a consolidated memory may inherit a constraint that was true when written and has since been withdrawn by a newer authoritative record. Under a scarce verification budget, does the agent recover the withdrawal, and if not, is the resulting stale-consistent decision avoidable without spending more? We model supersession explicitly -- provenance is immutable; what changes is which record is current -- and assign by design the memory's form, the world's state and the verification policy at a fixed budget of two records: the agent's own allocation, or the same budget with one slot re-assigned to the critical provenance path or to a random record. With a constraint stated, agents inspected its provenance path in about one episode in five; when that constraint had been superseded, native allocation produced stale-consistent decisions in 77.3%, 74.7% and 74.7% of episodes across a primary run, a fresh-wording replication and a held-out domain. Re-assigning one slot to the critical path raised current-record-consistent decisions by +74.0, +72.7 and +61.3 points, positive in six of six models in each run, and left an already near-ceiling rate unchanged when the record agreed with the memory. The held-out scenario was later found to contain a temporal inconsistency; a robustness replication with one sentence corrected, deposited externally before execution, gave +73.3 points (positive in 5 of six models, the sixth at a native missed-path rate of zero) and is reported alongside the original. The intervention uses knowledge of the critical path and is not a scheduler; it quantifies how much of the stale-consistent decision rate the bundled same-budget policy removes: the effect approaches the native missed-path rate in the primary, replication and corrected held-out runs. Memory systems may need freshness or supersession signals separate from relevance.
2608.25553.paper_summary_zh: 一個繼承了整合記憶的代理可能會繼承一個在寫入時為真的約束，而該約束自那時起已被更新的權威記錄撤回。在有限的驗證預算下，代理是否能恢復該撤回？如果不能，是否可以在不花費更多的情況下避免產生過時一致的決策？我們明確地對取代進行建模——來源是不可變的；改變的是哪個記錄是當前的——並設計記憶的形式、世界的狀態和在固定的兩條記錄預算下的驗證政策：代理自己的分配，或相同預算下的一個插槽重新分配給關鍵來源路徑或隨機記錄。在約束被陳述後，代理在約五次的實驗中檢查了其來源路徑；當該約束被取代時，本地分配在主要運行、新的措辭複製和保留域的實驗中產生了77.3%、74.7%和74.7%的過時一致決策。將一個插槽重新分配給關鍵路徑使當前記錄一致的決策提高了+74.0、+72.7和+61.3點，在每次運行中的六個模型中均為正數，並在記錄與記憶一致時保持了接近上限的比率不變。後來發現保留場景包含時間不一致性；一個修正了一句話的穩健複製，在執行前外部存放，給出了+73.3點（在六個模型中五個為正，六個在本地錯過路徑的比率為零），並與原始報告一起發布。該介入利用了關鍵路徑的知識，而不是調度器；它量化了捆綁的相同預算政策去除的過時一致決策率：該效果接近於主要、複製和修正保留運行中的本地錯過路徑率。記憶系統可能需要與相關性分開的新鮮度或取代信號。
2608.25553.author: Kazuki Nakayashiki et.al.
